university.name: Manav Rachna University (MRU)
university.vision: To educate students in frontier areas of knowledge enabling them to take up challenges as ethical and responsible global citizens.
mission: To impart outcome based holistic education
To disseminate education in frontier areas
To produce globally competitive, ethical and socially responsible human resources
To produce human resources sensitive to issues of Environment and Sustainable Development
To develop Environment and Sustainable development as a thrust area of research and development.

school.name: School of Engineering (SoE)
school.vision: To build a future where education and innovation, empowered by collaboration, create a sustainable global impact.
mission: SM1 Quality Education: Provide a rigorous, industry-aligned education that equips students with the foundational knowledge and technical expertise to excel in the academic and professional world.
SM2 Skill Development: Enhance skills by integrating hands-on learning experiences to promote critical thinking, problem-solving, and creativity.
SM3 Research and Innovation: Foster a culture of research and innovation that leads to new technologies and solutions to real-world problems.
SM4 Industry Collaboration: Build strong, strategic partnerships with industry leaders to bridge the gap between academic learning and real-world application.
SM5 Ethics and Sustainability: Nurture engineers to prioritize ethical decision-making for developing responsible solutions with a focus on a sustainable future.

CST.name: Department of Computer Science & Technology (DoCST)
CST.vision: To be a role model computer science department which imparts research based multidisciplinary competencies to foster innovation, creativity and ethical responsibility among students for transformative change in society and industry with sustainable solutions.
mission: DM1 Quality Education: Build student competency through industry-aligned curriculum delivered through relevant pedagogy and assessment.

DM2 Skill Development: Deploy employability skills in students by integrating hands-on learning labs experiences, interdisciplinary projects, and internships to imbibe critical thinking, problem solving, and creativity.
DM3 Research and Innovation: Collaborate with NI institutions and industry to foster a culture of research and innovation by supporting interdisciplinary projects.
DM4 Industry Collaboration: Build strong, strategic partnerships with industry for capacity building in innovation and real time knowledge.
DM5 Ethics and Sustainability: To produce ethical and socially responsible engineers who are allied with sustainable solutions for the industry.

ME.name: Department of Mechanical Engineering (DoME)
ME.vision: To be a center to nurture competent mechanical engineers equipped with strong technical knowledge, innovative thinking and ethical values, who contribute globally to industry, research and society through sustainable and future ready solutions.
mission: To provide quality education in mechanical engineering through an industry-aligned curriculum, hands-on learning, and modern pedagogical practices that foster technical excellence and lifelong learning.

To equip students with globally relevant technical and professional skills through hands-on training, internships, industrial exposure, and problem to project based learning, to make them ready for successful careers.
To cultivate a research-driven mindset by fostering innovation, multidisciplinary projects, and collaboration that address emerging challenges in science and technology
To nurture socially responsible engineers by instilling ethical values and environmental consciousness to make them industry ready to deliver sustainable engineering design and decision-making.
To strengthen industry-institute partnerships and community engagement for solving real-world problems, enhancing industrial relevance, and contributing to societal needs.

graduate_attributes.title: Engineering Knowledge
graduate_attributes.description: Breadth, depth and type of knowledge, both theoretical and practical
graduate_attributes.wa: Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing and engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop solutions to complex engineering problems.

graduate_attributes.title: Problem Analysis
graduate_attributes.wa: Identify, formulate, research literature and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences and engineering sciences with holistic considerations for sustainable development (WK1 to WK4).

graduate_attributes.title: Design/development of solutions
graduate_attributes.description: Breadth and uniqueness of engineering problems i.e., the extent to which problems are original and to which solutions have not previously been identified or codified
graduate_attributes.wa: Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design systems, components or processes to meet identified needs with appropriate consideration for public health and safety, whole-life cost, net zero carbon as well as resource, cultural, societal, and environmental considerations as required (WK5).

graduate_attributes.title: Investigation
graduate_attributes.description: Breadth and depth of investigation and experimentation
graduate_attributes.wa: Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research methods including research-based knowledge, design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of information to provide valid conclusions (WK8).

graduate_attributes.title: Tool Usage
graduate_attributes.description: Level of understanding of the appropriateness of technologies and tools
graduate_attributes.wa: Create, select and apply, and recognize limitations of appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools, including prediction and modelling, to complex engineering problems (WK2 and WK6).

graduate_attributes.title: The Engineer and the World
graduate_attributes.description: Level of knowledge and responsibility for sustainable development
graduate_attributes.wa: When solving complex engineering problems, analyze and evaluate sustainable development impacts to: society, the economy, sustainability, health and safety, legal frameworks, and the environment (WK1, WK5, and WK7).

graduate_attributes.title: Ethics
graduate_attributes.wa: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and norms of engineering practice and adhere to relevant national and international laws. Demonstrate an understanding of the need for diversity and inclusion (WK9).

graduate_attributes.title: Individual and Collaborative Team work
graduate_attributes.description: Role in and diversity of team
graduate_attributes.wa: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse and inclusive teams and in multi-disciplinary, face-to-face, remote and distributed settings (WK9).

graduate_attributes.title: Communication
graduate_attributes.description: Level of communication according to type of activities performed
graduate_attributes.wa: Communicate effectively and inclusively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, taking into account cultural, language, and learning differences.

graduate_attributes.title: Project Management and Finance
graduate_attributes.description: Level of management required for differing types of activity
graduate_attributes.wa: Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

graduate_attributes.title: Lifelong learning
graduate_attributes.wa: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change (WK8).

CSE.title: Core Competency
CSE.text: To inculcate analytical, design and implementation skills required to provide solutions to computing and interdisciplinary problems.

CSE.title: Breadth
CSE.text: To groom graduates to innovate, design and develop products to provide sustainable solutions to contemporary societal, environmental and business problems.

CSE.title: Professionalism
CSE.text: To instill the ability to work in teams, communicate effectively and lead as ethically and socially responsible professionals, researchers and entrepreneurs.

CSE.title: Life Long Learning
CSE.text: To foster the ability of lifelong learning to constantly adapt to emerging technologies, to pursue higher education and instill life skills for a successful career.

ME.text: Graduates will demonstrate strong technical knowledge and problem-solving skills in mechanical engineering, smart manufacturing, and electric vehicle technologies in their chosen career.
Graduates will pursue successful careers in global industries or as entrepreneurs by continuously upgrading their skills through modern tools and technologies.

Graduates will engage in research, innovation, and higher studies by applying modern tools, data-driven approaches, and interdisciplinary knowledge to address emerging technological challenges in mobility and manufacturing sector.
Graduates will practice engineering with a commitment to ethical values, sustainability, and societal well-being, contributing responsibly to the society.
Graduates will exhibit effective leadership, teamwork, and communication skills in multidisciplinary environments, enabling them to collaborate, manage, and deliver impactful engineering solutions.

pos.title: The Engineer and The World

pos.title: Ethics

pos.title: Individual and Collaborative Team work

pos.title: Communication

pos.title: Project Management and Finance
pos.text: Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

pos.title: Life-Long Learning
pos.text: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent and life-long learning ii) adaptability to new and emerging technologies and iii) critical thinking in the broadest context of technological change.

CSE.text: Attain the ability to design and develop computer programs and possess acquaintance with emerging technologies and open-source platforms in the area of mobile app development, artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative AI, web development, data analytics, cloud computing, networking, cyber security, quantum computing, gaming and animation to build effective computer-based systems.

Acquire technical competency to deliver computer based innovative and effective solutions to tackle business and societal challenges, for pursuing a successful career, entrepreneurship, research and higher studies.

ME.text: Students will be able to apply mechanical engineering tools and sustainable practices to analyze and solve engineering problems, considering technical, economic, environmental, and ethical aspects relevant to societal needs.
Students will be able to apply automation, CAD/CAM, sensors, industrial IoT, and data analytics to monitor, control and improve manufacturing processes in line with Industry 4.0 principles.

Students will be able to design, analyze, and implement key components of electric vehicle systems including electric drives, battery management systems, power electronics, and thermal systems (w.e.f July 2025)

WK.title: Natural Sciences
WK.text: A systematic, theory-based understanding of the natural sciences applicable to the discipline and awareness of relevant social sciences.

WK.title: Mathematics
WK.text: Conceptually-based mathematics, numerical analysis, data analysis, statistics and formal aspects of computer and information science to support detailed analysis and modelling applicable to the discipline.

WK.title: Engineering Fundamentals
WK.text: A systematic, theory-based formulation of engineering fundamentals required in the engineering discipline.

WK.title: Specialist Knowledge
WK.text: Engineering specialist knowledge that provides theoretical frameworks and bodies of knowledge for the accepted practice areas in the engineering discipline; much is at the forefront of the discipline.

WK.title: Engineering Design
WK.text: Knowledge, including efficient resource use, environmental impacts, whole-life cost, re-use of resources, net zero carbon, and similar concepts, that supports engineering design and operations in a practice area.

WK.title: Engineering Practice
WK.text: Knowledge of engineering practice (technology) in the practice areas in the engineering discipline.

WK.title: Comprehension
WK.text: Knowledge of the role of engineering in society and identified issues in engineering practice in the discipline, such as the professional responsibility of an engineer to public safety and sustainable development.

WK.title: Research Literature
WK.text: Engagement with selected knowledge in the current research literature of the discipline, awareness of the power of critical thinking and creative approaches to evaluate emerging issues.

WK.title: Ethics, inclusive behavior and conduct
WK.text: Knowledge of professional ethics, responsibilities, and norms of engineering practice. Awareness of the need for diversity by reason of ethnicity, gender, age, physical ability etc. with mutual understanding and respect, and of inclusive attitudes.

SK.title: Problem Solving
SK.text: Ability to identify, analyze, and solve complex engineering problems using logical reasoning and systematic methods.

SK.title: Design and Innovation
SK.text: Applying design thinking to develop creative, sustainable, and efficient engineering solutions.

SK.title: Use of Modern Tools
SK.text: Proficiency in tools such as CAD, simulation software, and data analytics to optimize engineering processes.

SK.title: Project Management
SK.text: Skills to manage projects effectively, including planning, execution, and monitoring of deliverables.

SK.title: Communication
SK.text: Clear and effective communication of ideas, designs, and reports to diverse audiences, including technical and non-technical stakeholders.

SK.title: Collaboration and Teamwork
SK.text: Working effectively in multidisciplinary teams to achieve shared objectives.

SK.title: Lifelong Learning
SK.text: Self-directed learning to stay updated with technological advancements and global trends.

SK.title: Research and Experimentation
SK.text: Skills to design experiments, analyze data, and apply research findings to engineering problems.

AK.title: Ethical Responsibility
AK.text: Commitment to ethical decision-making, integrity, and professional conduct in engineering practice.

AK.title: Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
AK.text: Respect for cultural, societal, and individual diversity, promoting inclusivity in engineering solutions.

AK.title: Sustainability Awareness
AK.text: Awareness of the need for sustainable development and the responsibility to minimize environmental impact.

AK.title: Global Awareness
AK.text: Understanding global challenges, such as climate change, and considering international perspectives in solutions.

AK.title: Accountability
AK.text: Taking responsibility for one's actions and decisions in professional practice.

AK.title: Leadership
AK.text: Inspiring and motivating teams to achieve shared goals with integrity and vision.

AK.title: Adaptability
AK.text: Embracing change, learning new tools, and adapting to evolving industry needs.

AK.title: Social Responsibility
AK.text: Commitment to contributing positively to society through engineering practices.

From Jan 2026: Slow Learners are those having an M-Score of less than 40% uptill Phase 1 of the semester (1 month into the semester) and Advanced Learners are those having an M-Score of greater than or equal to 75%). The remaining students are Moderate. Here, M-Score=C1*0.2+C2*0.8, where C1 is the aggregate marks of each student from the previous semester and C2 is the marks obtained for all assessments uptill Phase 1.
